description: Palak, commonly known as spinach, is a leafy green vegetable cultivated for its edible leaves. It is a popular crop for hydroponic systems due to its relatively fast growth cycle.
A fast-growing, cool-season crop. The plant forms a central rosette of leaves and can be harvested either as baby leaf or fully mature.
Leaves are typically dark green, broad, and can be smooth or savoyed (crinkled) depending on the variety. The leaf canopy expands laterally as the plant matures.

In Nutrient Film Technique (NFT), Palak is grown in channels with a shallow, continuous stream of nutrient solution. Root development is critical and is heavily influenced by flow rate and oxygenation.

As a cool-weather crop, it prefers moderate environmental conditions. Excessive heat can cause bolting (premature flowering) and negatively affect leaf quality. It requires adequate lighting but can tolerate partial shade.
Also commonly referred to as Indian Spinach or simply Spinach. In culinary contexts, it is widely used in South Asian cuisine.
Visual observation of the crop often focuses on leaf color, canopy size, and structural integrity. Yellowing or wilting leaves may indicate stress, nutrient imbalance, or disease.

Harvesting can be 'cut-and-come-again', where outer mature leaves are picked to allow inner leaves to continue growing, or a single whole-plant harvest. Maturity is generally gauged by leaf size and rosette fullness.
